writing.focus: nuanced inference and precise evaluation without overclaiming
writing.prompt: The table below shows the predicted chance of severe flooding and the actual outcome for three coastal towns in the country of Meridia over two storm seasons. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant. Write at least 150 words in about 20 minutes. Data: Predicted risk for 2022 season - Port Alan 60%, Dunmore 35%, Kestrel Bay 20%; Actual flooding in 2022 - Port Alan Yes, Dunmore No, Kestrel Bay No. Predicted risk for 2023 season - Port Alan 45%, Dunmore 40%, Kestrel Bay 30%; Actual flooding in 2023 - Port Alan No, Dunmore Yes, Kestrel Bay No. A survey note adds: 68% of residents in Port Alan said they ignored the 2023 warning because the 2022 warning had worried them unnecessarily.

writing.task: Task 1 · Comparing visitor access and conservation spending
writing.focus: competing evidence and scope limits in describing trends
writing.prompt: The charts below show visitor numbers (in thousands) and annual conservation spending (in thousand dollars) at two historic sites, Old Harrow Fort and Lina Temple, from 2019 to 2023. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant. Write at least 150 words in about 20 minutes. Data: Old Harrow Fort visitors - 2019: 120, 2020: 45, 2021: 80, 2022: 150, 2023: 180; spending - 2019: 200, 2020: 180, 2021: 190, 2022: 210, 2023: 220. Lina Temple visitors - 2019: 90, 2020: 30, 2021: 50, 2022: 70, 2023: 85; spending - 2019: 150, 2020: 160, 2021: 210, 2022: 260, 2023: 300. A site report notes minor wall damage increased at Old Harrow Fort in 2023, while Lina Temple reported no new damage.

writing.focus: causality limits and careful evaluation of competing approaches
writing.prompt: Some people argue that weather agencies should give a single clear warning even when forecasts are uncertain, while others believe agencies should explain the range of possible outcomes and how likely each is. Discuss both views and give your own opinion. Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience. Write at least 250 words in about 40 minutes.

writing.task: Task 2 · Whether universities should share research data
writing.focus: weighing competing evidence and scope of claims
writing.prompt: Many universities collect large sets of research data on topics such as climate, health, and agriculture. Some people think all publicly funded university research data should be freely shared with other researchers and the public, while others think universities should be allowed to restrict access to protect quality and future work. To what extent do you agree or disagree that publicly funded data should be openly shared? Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience. Write at least 250 words in about 40 minutes.

writing.task: Task 2 · Balancing access with conservation at historic sites
writing.focus: nuanced inference about causes and precise evaluation of solutions
writing.prompt: Historic sites attract many visitors, which supports local jobs but can damage old buildings and landscapes. Some suggest limiting visitor numbers and raising entry fees to protect these places, while others argue that historic sites belong to everyone and should remain fully open and affordable. Discuss both views and give your own opinion. Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience. Write at least 250 words in about 40 minutes.

speaking.task: Part 1 · Daily news and weather information
speaking.prompt: Part 1. I will ask you some questions about yourself and everyday life. How do you usually check the weather forecast? How often do you find forecasts uncertain or unclear? What do you do when a forecast says it might rain or storm? Do you think weather warnings in your area are easy to understand?

Part 1. Let us talk about historic places. Have you visited any old buildings, temples, or historic towns? What did you enjoy most about the visit? Do you prefer to visit popular historic sites or quieter, less-known ones? Would you be willing to book in advance if it helped protect a site?

speaking.task: Part 2 · Cue card: Explaining an uncertain forecast
speaking.focus: organised description with careful language about likelihood
speaking.prompt: Part 2. Take one minute to prepare and speak for one to two minutes. Describe a time when you heard an uncertain forecast about weather or the environment. You should say: • what the forecast was about and where you heard it • how the uncertainty was explained • what you and others decided to do • and explain whether you thought the communication was effective.

speaking.task: Part 2 · Cue card: A historic site you visited
speaking.focus: description balancing enjoyment and conservation awareness
speaking.prompt: Part 2. Take one minute to prepare and speak for one to two minutes. Describe a historic site you have visited or would like to visit. You should say: • where the site is and what is special about it • what visitors can see and do there • what problems too many visitors might cause • and explain how access and protection could be balanced at this site.

speaking.task: Part 3 · Sharing research and managing public knowledge
speaking.focus: reasons and evaluation, not memorised facts
speaking.prompt: Part 3. Let us discuss research and public information more generally. Why might universities hesitate to share their research data openly? What are the possible benefits and risks of making scientific data freely available? How should uncertain scientific findings be communicated to the public without causing confusion or panic? Who should be responsible for explaining limits in the evidence?
